message.content:
**How to kill Visual Studio Code (code.exe) from the command line**

On Windows you can terminate a running program with the built‑in `taskkill` utility.  
Below are the most common ways to stop VS Code (`code.exe`) safely and forcefully.

---

### 1. Kill *all* instances of `code.exe`

```cmd
taskkill /IM code.exe /F
```

* `/IM` – specifies the image name (process name).  
* `/F` – forces termination (equivalent to “kill -9” on Unix).

This will close every `code.exe` that is currently running, regardless of which user started it.

---

### 2. Kill a specific instance by PID

If you only want to close one particular VS Code window:

1. Find its Process ID (PID):

   ```cmd
   tasklist /FI "IMAGENAME eq code.exe"
   ```

   This lists all `code.exe` processes along with their PIDs.

2. Terminate the chosen PID:

   ```cmd
   taskkill /PID <PID_NUMBER> /F
   ```

   Replace `<PID_NUMBER>` with the actual number you saw in the previous step.

---

### 3. Using PowerShell (alternative)

If you prefer PowerShell, you can achieve the same with:

```powershell
Stop-Process -Name code -Force
```

or, to target a specific PID:

```powershell
Stop-Process -Id <PID_NUMBER> -Force
```

---

### Things to keep in mind

| Issue | What to do |
|-------|------------|
| **Multiple VS Code windows** | Each window runs as a separate `code.exe` process. `taskkill /IM code.exe /F` will close all of them. |
| **Administrator rights** | If VS Code was launched with elevated privileges, you may need to run the command prompt or PowerShell as Administrator. |
| **Unsaved work** | Force‑killing will not prompt you to save unsaved files. Use this only when you’re sure no important data will be lost. |

---

#### Quick cheat‑sheet

| Command | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| `taskkill /IM code.exe /F` | Close every VS Code instance immediately. |
| `tasklist /FI "IMAGENAME eq code.exe"` | List all VS Code processes and their PIDs. |
| `taskkill /PID <PID> /F` | Close a specific VS Code window by PID. |
| `Stop-Process -Name code -Force` | PowerShell equivalent of the first command. |

That’s it! Use whichever method fits your workflow. Happy coding (and killing)!
